line: Virtue, in the old sense of strength of character. The first will has been received and conceived, and now it settles into who you are; spring has come, and what was only force begins to flower. Drawn, the card speaks of a steady, harmonious beginning, a plan grounded enough to bear fruit, and integrity in how you act. The Sun, exalted in Aries, kindles Binah here, the great Mother, the sphere of Understanding.

quotes.quote: The Three of Wands is accordingly the Lord of Virtue. The idea of will and dominion has become interpreted in Character.
This card refers to Binah in the suit of Fire, and so represents the establishment of primeval Energy.

It refers to the Sun in Aries, the Sign in which he is exalted. The meaning is harmonious, for this is the beginning of Spring. For this reason one sees the wand taking the form of the Lotus in blossom. The Sun has enkindled the Great Mother.

These cards are referred to Binah; in each of them is expressed the symbolism of Understanding. The idea has become fertilized; the triangle has been formulated. In each case, the idea is of a certain stability which can never be upset, but from which a child can issue.
